summary: Canadian Coast Guard light on Reef Point at the entrance to Chance Harbour, New Brunswick. Station dates from 1915; the present cylindrical tower dates from about 1969.

structures.note: Square wooden tower completed in 1915 by day labourers under D. H. Mawhinney (LighthouseFriends). LighthouseFriends says it was replaced around 1969. The fate of the original is not stated.

Cylindrical tower. Rowlett gives 7.5 m (25 ft), a round fiberglass post painted red with a white band, dated 1969 (?). LighthouseFriends: red and white horizontal bands. Coast Guard list: white with a red band, 7.4 m.

staffing.note: LighthouseFriends: Frances Thompson served until the light was automated. No date is given.

access.note: Reached by a loop trail in Belding's Reef Nature Preserve (LighthouseFriends; Nature Trust of New Brunswick). Site open, tower closed (Rowlett).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); Nature Trust of New Brunswick (site manager, per Rowlett)

events.note: Bell buoy established off the harbour (Department of Marine, year ended 31 March 1913).
Day labourers under D. H. Mawhinney completed a square wooden tower on Reef Point (LighthouseFriends).
Nathan C. Belding first keeper, 1916 to 1950 (LighthouseFriends).

Two-masted Boston schooner Senator sprang a leak off Dipper Harbour, keeled over and was towed to the mouth of Chance Harbour. By 9 February 1922 she had capsized in the Bay of Fundy and lay off Chance Harbor (New York Herald, 3 February 1922; Daily Kennebec Journal, 10 February 1922).
Wreck of the schooner Senator removed by a departmental diver, and her masts, sunk off Chance Harbour, removed (year ended 31 March 1923).
Green can buoy placed 9 July 1923 marking the wreck of the schooner Senator at the western entrance to the harbour (year ended 31 March 1924).
Keeper Ronald Thompson drowned at the wharf in Chance Harbour, 15 December 1952 (LighthouseFriends).
Cylindrical tower replaced the original around 1969 (LighthouseFriends). Rowlett gives 1969 with a question mark.

keepers.name: Nathan C. Belding
keepers.note: First keeper of the light (LighthouseFriends). The Department's keeper tables read in the local corpus for 1900 to 1924 do not show him at Chance harbour; see notes_for_editor.

keepers.name: Ronald Thompson
keepers.note: Served as keeper after returning from the Second World War (LighthouseFriends). LighthouseFriends gives no start year. Drowned 15 December 1952 at the wharf in Chance Harbour.

keepers.name: Frances Thompson
keepers.note: Wife of Ronald Thompson. LighthouseFriends: took over responsibility for the light and served until it was automated. No end year given.

wrecks.outcome: Sprang a leak off Dipper Harbour in early February 1922, keeled over, was towed to the mouth of Chance Harbour and lay on her side off the harbour. The Department's reports for the year ended 31 March 1923 record the wreck and masts removed; a green can buoy was placed on 9 July 1923 to mark the wreck.

resolved_conflicts.field: status (record: a source says the structure is lost)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record cites LighthouseFriends as saying the structure is lost. The LighthouseFriends page read here says the cylindrical tower 'was still active in 2020', and no source read says the present tower is gone. The record keeps 'active'.

The Coast Guard list gives LFl W 6s (flash 2 s, eclipse 4 s), the record's value. Rowlett gives a white flash every 12 s; the record's OpenStreetMap value is LFl W 12s. The story gives the Coast Guard value and Rowlett's figure, and does not settle the difference.

LighthouseFriends: red and white horizontal bands. Rowlett: a round fiberglass post painted red with a white band. Coast Guard list: a white cylindrical tower with a red band. The story gives each account.

LighthouseFriends says the tower was completed in 1915; Rowlett gives the station as established in 1915. The record keeps 1915. Department reports for the years ended 31 March 1915 and 1916 list works at Chance harbour, including an 18-foot wooden lighthouse tower, but the lists are read by column position and the story does not use them (see notes_for_editor).

notes_for_editor: Sources: LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased, with short quotations); Rowlett; Coast Guard List of Lights (entry 93, page dated 2026-09-24); Nature Trust of New Brunswick; Department of Marine reports in the local corpus; New York Herald (3 Feb 1922, p. 19; also 10 Feb 1922, p. 18, which gives 'little hope of saving schr Senator, now lying on her beam ends off Chance Harbor'; not cited) and the Daily Kennebec Journal (10 Feb 1922, p. 10). The Senator's leak was 'yesterday' in a dispatch dated 2 February (the dateline OCR reads 'Feb 2?'), so the event is about 1 February 1922; the story says 'early February'. Identity of the Senator: the Herald says 'Boston schr Senator' and the Kennebec 'Boston-owned schooner Senator'; the Department's reports name 'schooner Senator' at Chance harbour in 1922-23 and 1923-24. Linked by name and place, not by a registry number. Keepers: Nathan C. Belding, Ronald Thompson and Frances Thompson appear only in LighthouseFriends. The Department's keeper tables read in the corpus (1900 to 1924) do not show Belding at Chance harbour. 'Robert L. Belding' is a keeper at Point Lepreau light in the keeper tables for 1904 to 1914 (fuzzy OCR), a different station and a different first name; the sources do not link him to Chance Harbour, and the story does not. Wallace Belding reportedly helped build the light: LighthouseFriends only. A web search also showed a Find a Grave memorial for a Ronald C. Thompson with the same 1952 death date; the search snippet was not read, so it is not cited. Tower completion: LighthouseFriends says 1915. The Department's 'Changes and Improvements in Existing Aids' lists for the years ended 31 March 1915 (corpus 1916v51i17p21_1196, 'Erection of 18-ft. wooden lighthouse tower') and 1916 (corpus 1917v52i13p21_1280, 'Completion of the erection of 18-foot wooden lighthouse tower') name Chance harbour among many stations, but the names and works sit in separate OCR columns. This story matches them by position only, so the story does not use them. The checker should read the page images before anyone attributes the tower to Chance harbour. Chance Harbour Breakwater Light and the Chance Harbour light buoy (Coast Guard entries 93.5 and 92.1 and 94) are separate aids and are not in this story. The Chance harbour bell buoy of 1913 is in the 1914 corpus volume (scan p. 94). Chronicling America search for 'Chance Harbor' in 1952-53 returned no hits. Living people: Frances Thompson's connection ended with automation, date unknown; she is named only as LighthouseFriends names her, with no personal detail beyond her role and her husband's death. Photographs: LighthouseFriends and Canadian Coast Guard photographs are not used; none with a clear licence was checked. Not checked: the Canadian Coast Guard's own automation records; the Nova Scotia and New Brunswick provincial archives (blocked in DESIGN section 2).
